limitations: Screens whether erosion-mediated particle transport is plausible; it does not estimate concentration, dose, risk, or regulatory acceptability.
Classification depends on user-supplied physicochemical evidence and coarse substance-class cues.
erosion_transport_relevance.applicabilityNote: Use before RUSLE/MUSLE when deciding whether sediment-associated transport is relevant for a soil release scenario.

rusle.displayName: Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation screening estimate
rusle.equationText: A = R * K * LS * C * P

sourceReferences.title: USDA NRCS Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation guidance

limitations: Returns long-term average annual soil loss for scalar screening.
Does not estimate event sediment yield, channel routing, deposition, receiving-water concentration, exposure, or risk.
rusle.applicabilityNote: Use RUSLE for erosion susceptibility or gross soil-loss screening when explicit R, K, LS, C, and P factors are available.

musle.displayName: Modified Universal Soil Loss Equation event sediment-yield estimate
musle.equationText: Sed = 11.8 * (Qsurf * qpeak)^0.56 * K * LS * C * P

sourceReferences.title: USACE HEC-HMS Technical Reference: Modified USLE

limitations: Requires caller-provided runoff volume and peak runoff rate.
Does not compute rainfall-runoff generation, hydrologic routing, calibration, receiving-water dilution, exposure, or risk.
musle.applicabilityNote: Use MUSLE when event runoff and peak-flow information are already available and a scalar sediment-yield screen is needed.

sourceReferences.title: USACE HEC-HMS Technical Reference: Modified USLE

limitations: Uses explicit caller-provided delivery and availability fractions.
Returns load only; it does not estimate receiving-water concentration, dose, exposure, risk, or regulatory acceptability.
sediment_associated_chemical_load.applicabilityNote: Use after MUSLE or another sediment-yield estimate when a bounded sediment-associated chemical-load handoff is needed.

sourceReferences.title: USDA NRCS Water Erosion Prediction Project

limitations: WEPP is not executed, reimplemented, or claimed equivalent inside this update.

deferredCapabilities: run WEPP when an operator-managed executable or service is configured
import WEPP output with version, parameter, and limitation provenance
wepp_deferred_adapter.applicabilityNote: Treat WEPP as a future external-model adapter path for process-based hillslope or small-watershed erosion simulation.
